title: Molecular docking and dynamics guided approach to identify potential anti-inflammatory molecules as NRF2 activator to protect against drug-induced liver injury (DILI): a computational study.
authors: Mili, Ajay; Das, Subham; Nandakumar, Krishnadas; Lobo, Richard
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MD模拟筛选NRF2激活剂以抗DILI，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作，但对象为KEAP1-NRF2蛋白-小分子体系，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress can contribute to the etiology of metabolic and chronic illnesses. The ability to prevent oxidative stress induced diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's disease, and others has been the subject of global research. Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) pathogenesis can be either due to oxidative stress or inflammatory response elicited by the drug, its metabolite, or herbal supplements. Our present research uses computational studies to identify a molecule with anti-inflammatory properties that can operate as an NRF2 activator. Acquiring and preparing the KEAP1-NRF2 Protein (PDB: 4L7D) with Schrodinger Suite was followed by developing a ligand library (Anti-inflammatory library downloaded from ChemDiv database). Molecular docking studies were performed in HTVS, SP, and XP modes, respectively. Based on the docking score, interaction, ADMET and binding free energy, the top ten compounds were selected and subjected to induced-fit docking (IFD) analysis for further study. The top three molecules were chosen for a molecular dynamics (MD) simulation study. Using the Desmond module of the Schrodinger Suite, the stability of the protein-ligand complex and protein-ligand contact throughout 100ns were evaluated during the MD simulation study. In our study, it was observed that three compounds exhibit exceptional stability and retain the essential interaction throughout the studies, and it is anticipated that these compounds may act as effective NRF2 activators. Further in vitro and in vivo assessments can be conducted to determine its potential to prevent DILI via acting as an NRF2 activator for future drug development.
abstract_zh: 炎症和氧化应激可促成代谢性疾病及慢性疾病的病因。预防由氧化应激诱导的疾病，如癌症、心血管疾病、阿尔茨海默病等，一直是全球研究的主题。药物性肝损伤（DILI）的发病机制可能源于药物、其代谢物或草药补充剂引发的氧化应激或炎症反应。我们当前的研究利用计算研究来识别一种具有抗炎特性、可作为NRF2激活剂的分子。获取并准备KEAP1-NRF2蛋白（PDB: 4L7D）使用Schrodinger Suite后，开发了一个配体库（从ChemDiv数据库下载的抗炎库）。分子对接研究分别在HTVS、SP和XP模式下进行。基于对接分数、相互作用、ADMET和结合自由能，选出了前十种化合物，并进行诱导拟合对接（IFD）分析以供进一步研究。选择前三种分子进行分子动力学（MD）模拟研究。使用Schrodinger Suite的Desmond模块，在MD模拟研究期间评估了100ns内蛋白-配体复合物及蛋白-配体接触的稳定性。在我们的研究中，观察到三种化合物表现出卓越的稳定性，并在整个研究过程中保留了关键相互作用，预计这些化合物可能作为有效的NRF2激活剂。可进一步进行体外和体内评估，以确定其通过作为NRF2激活剂预防DILI的潜力，为未来药物开发提供支持。
